column2: One can be turned away from a work without being aware that one is turned away from it.
Being turned away from a work is something an agent is answerable for when the agent could have turned back.
A turning away that began in ignorance becomes sin once it continues after knowledge, provided the agent, knowing, could turn back.
If knowledge of one's work is lost through one's own fault, a being turned away that continues can still count as sin; if it is lost without fault, it does not.
Standing facing a work as one's own is a condition that persists without continuous attention to the work.
Attention to a work can be sustained over time as a standing condition, not only given in moments.
Acknowledgment can be withheld throughout a sustained attention to one's own work.
Repentance is a process that can arrive at a condition, not only an act completed at once.
The standing facing that repentance arrives at can continue after the repentance itself has ended.
A standing condition, and not only a single act, can be given.
A facing can be partly given and partly achieved, so how far it is given can vary.
